profiles.summary: Public Polygon endpoints run Bor v2.11.1 and the newest release is v2.11.2 of 2026-11-19, which contains no hard fork. The only fork that is defined and not yet active is Hampi. It has no activation block and changes when SSTORE reads committed state, which alters block witnesses and leaves gas, results and state roots as they are.

deltas.delta: Hampi is wired dormant since Bor v2.10.1. Its single gate sits in core/vm/operations_acl.go and skips the committed state read of SSTORE when the frame cannot pay the access cost. The pull request states that gas charged, the out of gas outcome, receipts and state roots are identical with and without the gate. HampiBlock is nil for mainnet and Amoy on the master and develop branches.
deltas.source: https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/pull/2361

deltas.delta: The mainnet fork list on Bor master and develop ends with Austin 91949700 and Uburu 96787900, with Hampi unscheduled. No later fork field exists in params/config.go on either branch, so no public Bor fork is pending for the next six months as of 2026-11-23.
deltas.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/develop/params/config.go

deltas.delta: Bor v2.11.2 (2026-11-19) makes future Bor forks part of the eth fork ID and adds peer cleanup. Bor v2.11.1 (2026-11-13) is the public copy of v2.11.1-priv, a security release that validators ran before the source was public. The public endpoint used here reports v2.11.1-private.
deltas.source: https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/releases

profiles.summary: The consensus layer forked again on 2026-11-20 (Purley, Heimdall v0.14.0). The fork tightens how bridge events from Ethereum are confirmed before Bor executes them as state syncs. It went live on a private build and the source followed after activation, as with Uburu on Bor.

deltas.delta: Purley activated at Heimdall block 58,280,000 on 2026-11-20 01:39 UTC. Since then a validator's vote extension is carried signed in every block that includes it, and bridge events are confirmed before they are acted on. No Bor change was required. This narrows the path by which a state sync record reaches Bor, which is the path of finding F-010.
deltas.source: https://forum.polygon.technology/t/heimdall-v0-14-0-released-for-mainnet-and-amoy/22597

deltas.delta: Uburu (Bor, 2026-11-05), the security release v2.11.1 and Purley (Heimdall) were each distributed to validators as private builds, and the public source appeared at or after activation. A reviewer of the PoolManager cannot read a Polygon fork before it is live. The Uburu fork replaced the code of the genesis contract at 0x1001, so a fork can also replace the code at 0x1010.
deltas.source: https://forum.polygon.technology/t/announcement-bor-v2-11-0/22516

profiles.summary: This cycle listed every pool ever initialized on the Polygon PoolManager and tested all 7,456 pooled currencies for a shared balance. Two currency ids share one balance: the two addresses of Monerium EURe. One pool uses the native token contract 0x1010 as a currency and holds no liquidity. No other address reports the native balance.

deltas.delta: The PoolManager emitted 20,315 Initialize logs from block 67,012,640 to block 97,807,907. They name 7,456 distinct non-zero currency addresses and 328 hook addresses. At block 97,808,010 the PoolManager held a non-zero balance of 6,772 of these currencies. Two pooled currencies have no code (0x455e53cbb86018ac2b8092fdcd39d8444affc3f6 in two pools and 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead in one), and sync reverts for both on the deployed PoolManager.
deltas.source: rpc https://polygon.gateway.tenderly.co eth_getLogs in ranges of 1,000,000 blocks, and https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call and eth_getCode at block 97808010, 2026-11-23

deltas.delta: Monerium EURe answers at 0xE0aEa583266584DafBB3f9C3211d5588c73fEa8d (V2, a 170 byte ERC-1967 proxy) and at 0x18ec0A6E18E5bc3784fDd3a3634b31245ab704F6 (V1, 8,981 bytes, name Monerium EUR emoney). balanceOf(PoolManager) returns the same figure at both, 62,662.2 EURe at block 97,808,115 and 62,752.2 EURe at block 97,808,450. With Multicall3 code placed at the PoolManager address, a transfer of 1 EURe through the V2 address lowered the balance read at the V1 address by 1 EURe, and a transfer of 3 EURe through the V1 address lowered the balance read at the V2 address by 3 EURe. 27 pools use the V2 address and 21 pools use the V1 address.
deltas.source: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, blocks 97808115 to 97808450

deltas.delta: One pool with currency0 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 exists: pool id 0x79d1ed6dc35a3472253c1a5f4b13edfc1481e3b4bd70189c481cbf04b34cbf73, currency1 0x5eb10e40c4969dba42f344eb0cc2cd1a4bb3ad21 (symbol TESTSI COIN), fee 3000, tick spacing 60, no hook, initialized at block 70,895,654 in transaction 0xc379c9cb2f0c0b51fd792c8983c2b6ec091f7a23c3d85ba11bd077415886e443. StateView reports liquidity 0, the PoolManager holds none of currency1, and protocolFeesAccrued for 0x1010 is 0. No pool has 0x1010 as currency1.
deltas.source: rpc https://polygon.gateway.tenderly.co eth_getLogs with topic filters on currency0 and currency1 from block 60000000 to 97807856, and https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call on StateView 0x5ea1bd7974c8a611cbab0bdcafcb1d9cc9b3ba5a, 2026-11-23

deltas.delta: Among the 6,772 held currencies, 0x1010 is the only one whose balanceOf(PoolManager) equals eth_getBalance(PoolManager) (3,050,169.2 POL at block 97,808,010). 158 groups of currencies show identical non-zero PoolManager balances. A transfer of one base unit from the PoolManager was simulated for 814 members of these groups: only the EURe pair moved together, and 19 tokens rejected the transfer from the PoolManager.
deltas.source: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, blocks 97808010 to 97808115

profiles.summary: The special address sweep was repeated with the PoolManager as an inner frame. A forwarding stub at the PoolManager address, called by another account, sent 16 call shapes to 55 targets. Every answer equals the answer to a top level call sent as the PoolManager.

deltas.delta: Stub sweep at block 97,807,369: precompiles 0x01 to 0x11 and 0x0100, the genesis contracts 0x1000, 0x1001 and 0x1010, two burn contracts, the coinbase contract, FxChild, the ChildChainManager, WPOL, the token jar, the system address, the EIP-2935, EIP-4788, EIP-7002 and EIP-7251 addresses, Multicall3, CreateX, the deterministic deployer, three EntryPoints, the periphery, the owner and the fee controller. 0x1010 answered transfer of 0 with true, transfer of 1 with false, balanceOf under STATICCALL with the native balance and reverted on the other 13 shapes. The addresses of EIP-4788, EIP-7002 and EIP-7251 hold no code on Polygon and answer every shape with success and empty data.
deltas.source: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, block 97807369

deltas.delta: The V1 EURe address 0x18ec0A6E18E5bc3784fDd3a3634b31245ab704F6 has a fallback that accepts any unknown selector and empty calldata and returns success with no data. Calls of transfer_withCaller and approve_withCaller sent to it by an ordinary account succeeded and changed no balance and no allowance. The same calls sent to the V2 address revert.
deltas.source: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, block 97808450

profiles.summary: The public endpoints already run Geth v1.8.2, the Jenner client. The opcode fusion interpreter that earlier cycles could not locate was removed from the client in v1.8.0-alpha, so after 2026-12-08 no validating node can run it. Quoter simulations through the deployed PoolManager give identical results on v1.8.2, on v1.7.8 and on reth-bsc.

deltas.delta: v1.8.0-alpha removed the superinstruction feature of pull 3395 entirely (pull 3759): the interpreter, the fused opcodes and their jump table entries. The changelog lists four later changes to the feature while it existed (pulls 3582, 3584, 3622 and 3627), one of them titled superinstruction bad block. v1.8.2 is mandatory before Jenner, so the feature leaves the validator set on 2026-12-08 at the latest.
deltas.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/CHANGELOG.md

deltas.delta: 420 calls of quoteExactInputSingle and quoteExactOutputSingle on the deployed Quoter 0x95C086d7fE28AdD842ee220fef225a777474d781, for 15 pools of BNB, BSC-USD, USDC and WBNB, both directions and seven sizes from 10^12 to 10^27 base units, pinned to block 135,226,597. 409 answers, including the gas figure the Quoter measures, were identical on Geth v1.8.2, Geth v1.7.8 and reth-bsc v0.1.4. The other 11 were rate limited on the v1.7.8 endpoint and identical on the other two. 274 calls returned a quote and the largest measured 11,518,424 gas.
deltas.source: rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, https://bsc.blockrazor.xyz and https://bsc-rpc.publicnode.com, eth_call at block 135226597 on 2026-11-23

deltas.delta: After Jenner the precompile map gains 0x70, and every address that starts with 0xCA52 followed by eight zero bytes and a variant byte of 0 or 1, plus 0xCA5F000000000000000000000000000000000000, 0x7020000000000000000000000000000000000001 and 0x7020000000000000000000000000000000000002, is routed to native code. An address with that prefix and a variant byte of 2 or more is not routed and stays an ordinary account.
deltas.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/cas20.go

deltas.delta: The mainnet chain config sets JennerTime to 1796697000 and leaves AmsterdamTime, BPO1Time and BPO2Time nil. No fork after Jenner is scheduled.
deltas.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/params/config.go

profiles.summary: Jenner adds no system call and no transaction type. The three calls that the client makes from the system address still carry zero value, the payment lane reads its contract through the state database without running code, and the CAS20 native code never calls a contract. The probe of finding F-058 returns the same words on the Chapel testnet where Jenner is active.

deltas.delta: core/state_processor.go on master has three calls with From params.SystemAddress (lines 353 to 363, 380 to 390 and 420 to 429), each with value common.U2560. Parlia builds every system message with header.Coinbase as sender (consensus/parlia/parlia.go lines 1389, 2069, 2096, 2110, 2131 and 2137). parlia.go contains no reference to Jenner.
deltas.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/state_processor.go

deltas.delta: On Chapel at block 144,360,370 a call from 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe with value 7 and an overridden sender balance of 1000 reached a probe contract with CALLVALUE 7, left the probe balance at 100 and the sender at 1000. The same call from an ordinary address moved the 7 wei. BNB Smart Chain mainnet at block 135,226,408 gave the same result. The reth-bsc endpoint moved the 7 wei for the system address too, so the two clients disagree on a call that no transaction can make.

deltas.delta: BEP-703 is a block validity rule on gas totals. ResolveLaneState runs before the block EVM is created and passes only the state database to the package that reads the ratio and the contract list from 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000002007. The lane reserves 5 percent of the block gas limit by default and at most 10 percent for bare BNB transfers and for transactions to listed contracts. The mainnet block gas limit is 80,000,000 and the transaction cap stays at 16,777,216.
deltas.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/paymentlane/paymentlane.go

profiles.summary: CAS20 tokens exist on the Chapel testnet and behave toward a contract holder as the client source says: transfer returns a 32 byte true and moves exactly the amount, and a transfer policy that does not list the sender makes even a zero amount transfer revert. No CAS20 code reads or moves BNB. A sample of 1,364 currencies of recent mainnet pools shows no shared balance.

deltas.delta: On Chapel 33 CAS20Created logs were found in the last 6,000,000 blocks. For 12 tokens (4 of the Asset variant, 8 of the Stablecoin variant) Multicall3 code was placed at a holder address and called by another account: transfer(recipient, 1) returned a 32 byte true, the holder balance fell by 1 and the recipient balance rose by 1; transfer of 0 and a transfer to self returned true and changed nothing; a transfer above the balance reverted with selector 0xdb42144d; empty calldata reverted; decimals returned 18 for the Asset tokens and 6 for the Stablecoin tokens.
deltas.source: rpc https://bsc-testnet-dataseed.bnbchain.org (Chapel, chain id 97, Geth v1.8.1, Jenner active since 2026-10-29), eth_call with state override, blocks 144360009 to 144364040 on 2026-11-23

From an unlisted contract address, transfer of 0 and transfer of 1 both reverted with selector 0xa43fec12 (PolicyForbids). deltas.source: rpc https://bsc-testnet-dataseed.bnbchain.org (Chapel, chain id 97, Geth v1.8.1, Jenner active since 2026-10-29), eth_call with state override, blocks 144360009 to 144364040 on 2026-11-23

profiles.summary: No C-Chain rule change is scheduled. The next upgrade is named Igloo, has no activation time on Mainnet or Fuji, and the public work under that name moves Subnet-EVM chains to the new execution engine. ACP-209 is still in the Proposed state. The deployed periphery and all 282 hooks with code have no pair of constant storage slots that the C-Chain would fold into one.

deltas.delta: AvalancheGo v1.15.2 added the Igloo upgrade to the upgrade table with IglooTime set to UnscheduledActivationTime for Mainnet, Fuji and the default config. The open epic for Igloo describes a Continuous Execution VM for L1 chains that replaces Subnet-EVM. No public issue or source file gates a C-Chain opcode, precompile or transaction type on Igloo.
deltas.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/master/upgrade/upgrade.go

deltas.delta: ACP-209 remains Proposed and has no reference implementation. Its text adds set code transactions and a ReservedBalanceManager precompile at 0x0200000000000000000000000000000000000006 with a payable depositReservedBalance(address) that any account can call for any account. Contract code would see only the regular balance. The address holds no code and answers every call with success and empty data today.
deltas.source: https://github.com/avalanche-foundation/ACPs/blob/main/ACPs/209-eip7702-style-account-abstraction/README.md

findings.title: Monerium EURe sits in the Polygon PoolManager under two currency ids that share one balance, and the issuer can retire the legacy address
findings.difference: On Polygon the e-money token EURe answers at two addresses that share one ledger. The V2 token is an ERC-1967 proxy at 0xE0aEa583266584DafBB3f9C3211d5588c73fEa8d. The V1 address 0x18ec0A6E18E5bc3784fDd3a3634b31245ab704F6 (name Monerium EUR emoney) has forwarded transfer, transferFrom, approve and balanceOf to V2 since the upgrade of 2024-08-18 at block 60,733,237. Both addresses report the same balance for every holder, and a transfer through either one lowers the balance read at both. The same pair exists on Ethereum (V1 0x3231Cb76718CDeF2155FC47b5286d82e6eDA273f, V2 0x39b8B6385416f4cA36a20319F70D28621895279D). The PoolManager code treats every address as a separate currency with a separate balance.
findings.mechanism: 1. A currency id is the token address, and deltas, ERC-6909 claims and accrued protocol fees are recorded per address (src/types/Currency.sol:110-118, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41, src/ProtocolFees.sol:21). 2. On Polygon 27 pools were initialized with the V2 address and 21 pools with the V1 address. At block 97,808,450 fourteen of the V2 pools and two of the V1 pools had active liquidity, the PoolManager held one balance of 62,752.2 EURe, and protocolFeesAccrued was 77.59 EURe under the V2 id and 2.27 EURe under the V1 id. 3. Walk of the ordinary caller across the two ids. sync stores one currency and one reserve figure (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), so two snapshots cannot be open at once. A payment between sync and settle is credited once, to the id that is synced at that moment (src/PoolManager.sol:349-365). A take debits its own id and lowers the shared balance (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). Example: take 100 EURe under the V1 id, sync the V2 id, send the 100 EURe back, settle. The caller now holds a credit of 100 under the V2 id and still owes 100 under the V1 id, so the sum of credits equals the sum paid in. A take or a fee collection under one id between sync and settle of the other id lowers the measured rise, which under-credits the settling caller or reverts at src/PoolManager.sol:360. mint and burn use separate ids (src/PoolManager.sol:322-336). No order of sync, settle, take, mint and burn credits one payment twice, so the two ledgers stay jointly covered by the one balance. 4. The hazard sits with the issuer. The V1 address and the V2 proxy have the same owner, 0x8001ea269cb9715bf7acff89c664ffc134a519ec. getController() on the V1 address returns the V2 address, and the V1 bytecode holds the selector of setController(address). If Monerium disconnects the V1 address, points it at another controller or changes how V2 serves its frontend, transfer and balanceOf at the V1 address fail or stop following the shared ledger. take for the V1 id then reverts at src/types/Currency.sol:82-86, and sync for the V1 id fails or reads another figure. The tokens stay in the PoolManager and remain payable only under the V2 id, to parties that hold V2 deltas. Core has no function that converts a pool balance or a claim from one currency id to another. 5. The guard in collectProtocolFees compares addresses (src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-52), so it does not stop a collection of V2 fees while the V1 id is synced. The fee controller on Polygon lets any account trigger collection. The effect stays inside the transaction of the party that is settling and costs that party the collected amount or a revert.
findings.impact: Funds owed under the V1 id: an unknown share of about 62,750 EURe, in 21 pools of which two have active liquidity, plus 2.27 EURe of accrued protocol fees. If the V1 address stops working these funds cannot leave the PoolManager until the issuer restores it. Liquidity providers could still remove liquidity and hold ERC-6909 claims of the V1 id, which have no payout path. Indexers and risk tools that read balanceOf per currency id count this balance twice. No funds of other pools are affected and no ordinary account gains anything.
findings.preconditions: Monerium, through the owner account of both contracts, must change or disconnect the V1 address or upgrade V2. Monerium states that V1 continues to be supported and that it works with protocols to move liquidity to V2. No ordinary account can trigger the freeze. The split of the balance between the two ids was not computed.
findings.mitigations: Interfaces, routers and token lists on Polygon should offer only the V2 address 0xE0aEa583266584DafBB3f9C3211d5588c73fEa8d and warn on pools that use 0x18ec0A6E18E5bc3784fDd3a3634b31245ab704F6. Liquidity providers in V1 pools can move to V2 pools while both addresses work. Indexers should treat the two ids as one balance. The deployment notes for Polygon and Ethereum should name both pairs.

findings.title: Jenner client source and the Chapel testnet show how a CAS20 issuer can block or seize the PoolManager balance, and seizure needs one more step than first recorded
findings.difference: BNB Smart Chain activates Jenner at timestamp 1796697000 (2026-12-08 02:30 UTC). The client then runs CAS20 tokens as native code behind addresses that start with 0xCA52. Each token carries roles for mint, burn, seize, pause and metadata, a pause mask per feature, and six policy lanes that point at shared allowlists and blocklists in a policy registry. The standard is live on the Chapel testnet since 2026-10-29. Ethereum has no token logic in the client.
findings.mechanism: 1. transfer checks the pause bit, then the sender policy and the receiver policy, then debits the sender and credits the recipient by the amount and returns a 32 byte true (core/vm/cas20_token.go lines 175 to 189 and 239 to 269). The PoolManager accepts that answer (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). 2. A policy that does not authorize the sender makes transfer revert with PolicyForbids for every amount, zero included. On Chapel the token 0xca52000000000000000001217954ab5467577565 has sender policy 0x0100000000000007, and transfer of 0 and of 1 from an unlisted contract address both reverted with selector 0xa43fec12. If the token admin binds TRANSFER_SENDER_POLICY to a list that leaves the PoolManager out, if the admin of that list removes the PoolManager, or if PAUSE_ROLE pauses the transfer feature, then every take and every protocol fee collection in that token reverts (src/types/Currency.sol:82-86, src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/ProtocolFees.sol:56). 3. A receiver policy that leaves the PoolManager out makes every payment to it revert, so settle credits nothing (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). The transfer reverts and the amount is not diverted to another account. 4. seizeWithMemo needs SEIZE_ROLE and an unpaused seize feature, and it refuses a source that the SEIZE_EXEMPT policy authorizes (core/vm/cas20_admin.go lines 507 to 553). The default policy id 0 authorizes every account, so with default settings no account can be seized. The admin must first bind SEIZE_EXEMPT_POLICY to a list that leaves the PoolManager out. After that an account with SEIZE_ROLE can move the PoolManager balance to any allowed receiver without a take, and the pools still record the old amounts. The earlier text of this finding named a scope SEIZE_HOLDER_POLICY and a blocklist that contains the PoolManager. The client names the scopes SEIZE_EXEMPT_POLICY and SEIZE_RECEIVER_POLICY, and the test is the inverse: exemption must be withdrawn. 5. balanceOf returns the raw balance. The Asset multiplier is applied only by the UI selectors, so it causes no rebase at the PoolManager. A call that cannot pay for a storage read ends with an out of gas error and does not return a zero balance (core/vm/cas20_errors.go lines 55 to 63), so sync cannot record a false zero. 6. Token creation and policy creation are closed until an administrator appointed through GovHub 0x1007 activates them (core/vm/cas20_activation.go). On Chapel all three features are active.
findings.impact: All reserves, ERC-6909 claims and protocol fees that the PoolManager holds in an affected CAS20 token. A policy change or a pause freezes them until the issuer reverses it. A seizure after the exemption is withdrawn is a loss for the liquidity providers of those pools. None of this applies today on mainnet because no CAS20 token can exist before the fork and before activation.
findings.preconditions: Jenner activates, the activation administrator opens token creation on mainnet, a CAS20 token is created and pooled, and the roles of that token act as described. An ordinary account can do this only with a token it issued itself, which harms only those who pool that token.
findings.mitigations: Before a CAS20 token is listed, read policyId for the six scopes, isPaused for the four features, and the holders of SEIZE_ROLE, PAUSE_ROLE and the admin role. A token whose sender or receiver policy is an allowlist cannot be pooled unless the PoolManager and the routers are on it. Prefer tokens whose SEIZE_EXEMPT policy is the default and whose admin role was renounced. After 2026-12-08 repeat the Chapel checks of this cycle on mainnet.

findings.title: One Polygon pool already uses the native token contract 0x1010 as a currency, it holds no liquidity, and the inner frame tests leave the finding unchanged
findings.difference: Polygon has a genesis contract at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 whose balanceOf returns the native POL balance of an account and whose transfer returns false unless msg.value equals the amount. Ethereum has no ERC-20 face of its native asset in the protocol.
findings.mechanism: 1. The precondition that someone initializes a pool with 0x1010 has been met once. Pool 0x79d1ed6dc35a3472253c1a5f4b13edfc1481e3b4bd70189c481cbf04b34cbf73 pairs 0x1010 with the token 0x5eb10e40c4969dba42f344eb0cc2cd1a4bb3ad21 since block 70,895,654. It has zero liquidity, the PoolManager holds none of the other token, and no protocol fee accrued under 0x1010. 2. From a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address, called by another account, 0x1010 answered transfer of 0 with true, transfer of 1 with false, balanceOf under STATICCALL with the native balance, and reverted on value calls, on the ten hook selectors and on unlockCallback. This equals the top level results of cycles 1 and 2, so take of a non-zero amount still fails the success test at src/types/Currency.sol:64-74. 3. Among all 6,772 currencies that the PoolManager holds, 0x1010 is the only one whose balanceOf equals the native balance, so no second address measures POL. 4. Walk across the two ids. sync(0x1010) records the native balance. A native settle with value then reverts at src/PoolManager.sol:356. sync(address(0)) clears the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283), and a later sync(0x1010) reads the balance again, so the stored reserve is never older than the last native credit. A native take or a native fee collection between sync(0x1010) and settle lowers the balance and makes settle revert at src/PoolManager.sol:360. A credit under 0x1010 therefore still needs POL that reached the PoolManager without a call, and it still cannot be paid out.
findings.impact: Unchanged. POL forced into the PoolManager and booked under 0x1010 cannot leave as that currency. The one existing pool holds nothing. Pools that hold POL under address(0) are not affected.
findings.preconditions: A custom contract must force POL into the PoolManager between sync and settle. The actor loses its own funds. No path takes funds of other users.
findings.mitigations: Interfaces and indexers on Polygon should refuse 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 as a pool currency and should flag the existing pool. The probe of 0x1010 should be repeated after every Bor fork, because forks can replace genesis contract code and recent forks were distributed privately.

cleared.check: Lead L-209 and L-332: do the special addresses answer the PoolManager differently when it is an inner frame with another transaction origin? A 69 byte forwarding stub was placed at the PoolManager address by state override and called by 0x00000000000000000000000000000000c0ffee01. Sixteen shapes per target: empty calldata with 1 wei and with zero value, transfer of 0 and of 1, balanceOf(PoolManager) under STATICCALL, the ten IHooks selectors and unlockCallback. 55 targets on Polygon, 75 on BNB Smart Chain, 56 on Avalanche. Each shape was also sent as a top level call with from set to the PoolManager at the same block.
cleared.result: No difference on any of the three chains. The stub and the direct call gave the same success flag and the same return data for every shape and target. The only mismatches are artefacts: the PoolManager address itself holds the stub in the stub run. No target returns 32 bytes that start with a hook selector, so none passes the response test at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154. A 32 byte true comes back only from token contracts (the wrapped native tokens, and 0x1010 for amount zero). Success with empty data comes from accounts without code and from precompiles that return nothing for this input, which is the known case where take debits the caller and moves nothing (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). Value calls succeed at accounts without code, at several precompiles, at the wrapped native tokens and at contracts with a receive function such as the routers, the PositionManager, the EntryPoints and the burn and fee contracts. The caller of take is debited the full amount in each case (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297).

cleared.check: Lead L-261 and L-332: which entry points of the Jenner native code can an account without a role call, can any of them change another holder's balance, can transfer succeed without lowering the caller's balance, and does any CAS20 address report the native BNB balance? Read of cas20.go, cas20_token.go, cas20_admin.go, cas20_asset.go, cas20_stablecoin.go, cas20_permit.go, cas20_memo.go, cas20_factory.go, cas20_policy.go, cas20_activation.go, cas20_errors.go, cas20_storage.go and contracts_stateful.go on master, plus calls on Chapel.
cleared.result: An account without a role can call the views, approve, transfer, transferFrom, permit and the memo variants of a token, the read functions of the registries and, once the feature is activated, createCAS20, createPolicy and createCompositePolicy. transfer and transferFrom debit the named source by the amount and credit the recipient, and transferFrom needs an allowance of the source. mint, burn, seizeWithMemo, pause, updatePolicy, updateSupplyCap and the multiplier setters each need a role. The factory runs its init calls with elevated rights, and those calls act only on the storage of the token being created, whose address must hold no code. transfer returns success only after the debit, except for a zero amount and for a transfer to self. Every successful transfer returns a 32 byte true and never empty data. balanceOf reads the token ledger and returns 0 for an address that holds only BNB. No CAS20 file reads or writes a native balance or calls a contract, and every entry point reverts when value is attached. The millisecond timestamp precompile 0x70 ignores its input and returns one 32 byte word that is constant within a block.
cleared.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/cas20_token.go and the sibling files named in the check; rpc https://bsc-testnet-dataseed.bnbchain.org (Chapel, chain id 97, Geth v1.8.1, Jenner active since 2026-10-29), eth_call with state override, blocks 144360009 to 144364040 on 2026-11-23

cleared.check: Upcoming fork: what changes for the PoolManager on 2026-12-08 at the addresses that Jenner turns into native code, and can any pool, claim or fee already exist under those addresses? Compared mainnet answers before the fork with Chapel answers after it.
cleared.result: Before the fork the CAS20 range, the three singleton addresses, 0x2007 and 0x70 answer every call with success and empty data. A take that names one of them as currency succeeds, moves nothing and debits the caller (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). sync reverts for them, because the balanceOf call returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:94), so no credit, no liquidity and no claim can exist under these ids today. After the fork the singleton addresses, 0x2007 and uncreated token addresses of variant 0 and 1 revert on every shape, so take and sync both revert. 0x70 answers balanceOf and transfer with the millisecond timestamp: sync succeeds, settle credits zero because the word is constant within a block (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and take reverts because the word is not 1. As a hook address 0x70 has the flags afterSwap, beforeDonate and afterDonate, and its answer fails the selector test at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154 before and after the fork. The fork therefore changes no balance and no claim of the deployed PoolManager.

cleared.result: No on both counts. move checks the sender policy and the receiver policy and reverts with PolicyForbids when either fails. On success it writes exactly two balance slots, the source and the named recipient. There is no escrow, no pending credit and no recovery account. Chapel confirmed the revert for a token with a sender policy and the exact credit for 12 tokens. No CAS20 code touches a BNB balance.

cleared.check: Faces on Polygon: walk of sync, settle, take, mint, burn and protocol fee collection across the two EURe addresses and across address(0) and 0x1010, in every order, for an ordinary caller.
cleared.result: No order credits one payment twice or pays out more than was credited. sync holds one currency and one reserve figure at a time (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32). settle credits only the rise of the synced currency's balance since that sync (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and a native settle is refused while a token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356). take debits the id it names before it transfers (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295). A take or a fee collection of the other face between sync and settle lowers the measured rise and costs the settling caller. mint and burn act on separate claim ids (src/PoolManager.sol:322-336). A standing surplus cannot be claimed, because sync always starts from the current balance. The hazards that remain are the issuer hazard recorded for EURe and the dead credit recorded for 0x1010.

cleared.check: Upcoming fork on Polygon: does the dormant Hampi fork or any scheduled Bor fork change what the PoolManager bytecode computes?
cleared.result: No. Hampi has no activation block and its single gate changes only whether SSTORE reads committed state before an out of gas exit. Gas charged, results and state roots stay the same according to the pull request and its tests. Bor master and develop define no fork after Uburu. A fork distributed privately, as Uburu was, could not be reviewed in advance.

cleared.check: Upcoming fork on Avalanche: does Igloo or ACP-209 change what an ordinary account can make the PoolManager do in the next six months?
cleared.result: Nothing is scheduled. IglooTime is unscheduled on Mainnet and Fuji, and its public scope is the move of L1 chains to the Continuous Execution engine. ACP-209 is Proposed without an implementation. If it ships as written, delegated accounts become possible as hooks (the case of finding F-004), and any account could deposit AVAX into the reserved balance of the PoolManager, which contract code cannot see or spend. Neither changes settle, which credits msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354).

cleared.check: Upcoming fork: does the BEP-703 payment lane move balances, pay fees in tokens or change how PoolManager transactions are priced?
cleared.result: No. The lane is one inequality on gas totals per block. It reserves 5 percent of the block gas limit by default, at most 10 percent, for bare BNB transfers to accounts without code and for transactions to contracts that governance lists. A PoolManager transaction is a general transaction and competes for the remaining 90 to 95 percent of an 80,000,000 gas block. The transaction cap of 16,777,216 gas is unchanged, and the largest Quoter simulation of this cycle used 11,518,424 gas.

cleared.check: Can a CAS20 balanceOf call that runs short of gas return zero, so that sync records a false zero reserve and settle credits the whole balance?
cleared.result: No. A storage read that cannot be paid returns a zero word inside the native code and sets a sticky out of gas flag. finishCAS20Metered checks that flag before it returns data and ends the call with ErrOutOfGas, which the EVM reports as a failed call. The high level balanceOf call at src/types/Currency.sol:94 then reverts.

A take of a non-zero amount would leave a debt that cannot be settled and the unlock reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:112).

leads.question: Which contract sends ANTB (0x38dd26788cf2d901e3abf04efe3007d459d0fc53) to the PoolManager when BUTTHOLE (0x020e5f774ca2e84fc80612b2c8503413a549ffff) is transferred from it, how much has accumulated, and can an account book it with sync, a zero amount take and settle?
leads.why: A balance that rises on a third party trigger is the pattern of findings F-060 and F-066. The simulated inflow was 25,751,442,464,642 base units for one transfer, which is small, and other launch platform tokens on the chain may pay larger amounts.

leads.question: After each Bor fork: does the code at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 still return false for transfer without value, and does any new genesis contract or precompile report or move native POL?
leads.why: Uburu replaced the code at 0x1001 at the fork block and reached validators as a private build. A change that let 0x1010 move POL without value would turn the dead credit of finding F-008 into a working second face of the native asset. The existing guard at src/PoolManager.sol:356 would then carry the same weight as on Celo.

leads.question: Do any two pooled currencies share a balance in different units (for example a share token and its underlying read through one ledger), beyond the 170 most pooled tokens per chain?
leads.why: The equal balance grouping finds only faces with a one to one unit. The group test for other ratios was limited to 170 tokens by the 100,000 byte cap on return data. A probe contract that returns one changed flag per token would lift the limit.

leads.question: When the C-Chain rule set for Igloo is published: does it include ACP-209, a new precompile at 0x0200000000000000000000000000000000000006, new opcodes or a change to the storage partition rule of finding F-040?
leads.why: Igloo is the only named upgrade and has no public C-Chain scope. Set code accounts and a precompile that takes value for a named account are the two parts of ACP-209 that meet the PoolManager call shapes.

leadResults.answer: Read the Jenner native code on master and exercised it on Chapel. Accounts without a role reach the token views, approve, transfer, transferFrom, permit, the memo variants, the registry views and, after activation, the creation functions. None of them changes another holder's balance without that holder's allowance or signature. transfer returns a 32 byte true only after it debited the caller by the amount (a zero amount and a transfer to self leave the balance as it was), and it never returns empty data. balanceOf returns the token ledger value, which is 0 for an address that holds only BNB. No CAS20 file calls a contract, uses the system address as a caller or handles value: every entry point reverts with NonPayable when value is attached. Precompile 0x70 returns the block's millisecond timestamp for any input.

Repeated the sweep with a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address on Polygon (55 targets, block 97,807,369), BNB Smart Chain (75 targets, block 135,226,007) and Avalanche (56 targets, block 101,141,646) for the sixteen shapes. No answer differs from the top level call. This closes lead L-209 for the three chains. From cas20.go and contracts_stateful.go and from Chapel: after 2026-12-08 an uncreated address of variant 0 or 1 in the CAS20 range reverts on all sixteen shapes, a created token answers transfer with a 32 byte true and balanceOf with its ledger value and reverts on the rest, addresses with a variant byte of 2 or more stay accounts without code, and 0x70 answers every shape with one timestamp word. No CAS20 address reports the native BNB balance.

Jenner adds no system call and no transaction type. The client still makes three calls from 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe, each with zero value and a fixed target, Parlia sends system messages from the coinbase, and the CAS20 and payment lane code run no contract. The probe returned the same words on Chapel with Jenner active (CALLVALUE 7, no balance moved) and on mainnet. The reth-bsc client moves the value for that caller, a disagreement on a call that no transaction can produce.

From the client source and from 12 live tokens on Chapel: transfer returns a 32 byte true and moves exactly the amount, balanceOf returns 32 bytes and works under STATICCALL, a transfer above the balance reverts with InsufficientBalance, and a policy that does not list the sender or the recipient makes the transfer revert for every amount. sync, settle and take therefore work with a CAS20 token whose policies admit the PoolManager. Token creation on mainnet stays closed after the fork until an administrator appointed through GovHub activates it. No CAS20 token can have a pool before 2026-12-08, and a new lead asks for the list after activation.

BNB Smart Chain part: no. No CAS20 token, singleton or reserved address reads or moves a native BNB balance, all of them reject value, and 0x70 returns a timestamp. BNB gets no second face from Jenner. The Base part of the lead belongs to another unit and was not examined.

BNB Smart Chain part: the CAS20 code has no path on which transfer returns true while the amount is credited elsewhere. A receiver or sender policy failure reverts the transfer with PolicyForbids, and a success writes the source and the named recipient only. No guard contract and no recovery account exist in the design. The Base and Robinhood Chain parts belong to other units and were not examined.

The superinstruction feature was removed from the client in v1.8.0-alpha (pull 3759) and cannot run on any validator after Jenner, for which v1.8.2 is mandatory. Until then validators on v1.7.x may still run it. 420 Quoter simulations through the deployed PoolManager at one block gave 409 identical answers on Geth v1.8.2, Geth v1.7.8 and reth-bsc, and the remaining 11 were rate limited on one endpoint and identical on the other two. Open parts: whether the v1.7.8 endpoint has the optimisation enabled, and the list of fused sequences, since the v1.7 source was not read.

No. The PositionManager, PositionDescriptor, Quoter, StateView, ReservesLens, the three Universal Routers, Permit2 and the owner contract on Avalanche, and all 282 hooks with code named by the 5,779 Initialize logs, hold no two PUSH32 constants that differ only in bit 248. The test reads constants in bytecode and does not cover slots computed at run time.
